title: I'm only seeing Opus5.5 posts!
author: eragon1man
selftext: Hey yall! Just curious! Has anybody had success or has any demos of creating 3d games using any ChatGPT models? I ask because that is what I have right now so I'm looking to see if other people have had success with it. I've mostly been seeing Opus and Blender combos on here.

comments.author: RuinousFate
comments.body: We'd tell you but ChatGPT is so slow its still finishing my first prompt from when Sol 6.1 released!

comments.author: BroEvenIDK
comments.body:
Sol 6.1 aint that good at these 3D games (no taste like opus)  
Astra is good (assuming it’s not needed like ppl r claiming) but the average user can’t really built out full games by vibecoding unless they’re also doing some chunk of work manually cuz the usage limits r js so bad

replies.author: BroEvenIDK
replies.body: \*\*It’s not nerfed\*\*\* DK how that autocorrected

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body:
6.1 is not so great at making things from scratch. It can, but yeah no taste. What I have found it useful for is drudge work that isn't completely mindless. I have a set of like 100 mocap clips that needed to be ingested, matched to the rig and cleaned for foot placement and offset (monocular footage) and it did an admirable job of that for basically nothing. 

Totally capable of doing things. Not so great at making things.

replies.author: KharusVII
replies.body: Wait… you used sol 6.1 to clean up mocap?!

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body: Clean is a stretch. A lot of it still needs a manual signoff. What it did do is correct feet placement, body alignment from the bad mocap, timestamp sections of the roll and create clean start and stop loops.

comments.author: fued
comments.body: I use Luna because I'm cheap lol

comments.author: Legal_Steak_4609
comments.body: I'm using Terra 5.6, it's good enough and quite fast. Sol 6.1 is way too expensive. Occasionally review the code with Astra or Fable.

replies.author: pizzaisprettyneato
replies.body: I’m pretty sure Terra and 6.1 sol are the same price.

replies.author: Legal_Steak_4609
replies.body: Sol seems to consume much more tokens for similar coding tasks. I ran out of my usual monthly quota in under a week.

comments.author: Mental-Frosting-7752
comments.body: Codex in general is not in a good place right now price gouging wise and quality, i lowered my sub to just the 20$ one for image gen access and have Opus utilize generated concept models from Image gen and build out my assets

comments.author: Easy-Coconut-33
comments.body: Im using deepseek 4.1 for the code and calling Claude when i need help with the bigger task. Working great so far.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body:
I was all codex until a week ago I tried Opus 5.5 and holy crap it’s good. It has taste and is good at art direction and level design. Only issues I have with it is it’s very over eager and will often start work if I’m not very explicit that we’re still planning. It goes above and beyond and tries to add things it things you’ll want which is great when it guesses right but can be a pain when you have to get it to back things out. But overall it tends to delight with unexpected details.

I now use codex when I have a well scoped coding task and I use Claud for more open ended coding tasks and art and level design.

comments.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
comments.body: Opus goes the extra mile and Sol does the bare minimum. Can't speak on Astra/Fable but Sol vs Opus is not even close.

comments.author: kenny32vr
comments.body: Becaus opus 5.5 is crazy good at making games . Even sonnet 5.5 seem good

comments.author: Seerix
comments.body:
Sol 6.1 and Astra are both great models but they are *slow* right now. And astra use is extremely expensive. Claude Opus on the other hand... If you only use a single agent I dont think you can run out on the $100 plan.

I'm using both for my game. Opus 5.5 is my primary, and I use Astra to assist with texture + model work. $100 plan for both.

comments.author: reality_comes
comments.body: Astra really paved the way, but 5.5 blew it away, entry cost is the same so no reason not to use 5.5

comments.author: dazreil
comments.body: Opus 5.5 is the goat. Open AI have slashed the usage allowance and Sol 6.1 is a fucking glutton.

comments.author: DudeWithASweater
comments.body: I actually prefer chatgpt for image generation for my assets. I find it does a better job for what I'm looking for. I then give them to Claude and it codes the game

comments.author: Icy-Fudge5222
comments.body: Astra is too expensive for what it does, and SOL 6.1 just doesn't do the work as well as Sonnet or OPUS. I will say that Codex seems better at pulling data from the web. I wanted to pull some GIS and other public-facing city data, and Claude struggled while giving a lot of pushback. I ended up having Codex pull whatever data Opus needed and feeding it to Opus to use.
